title: Steering Visual Generation in Unified Multimodal Models with Understanding Supervision
claim: Adding understanding supervision to a baseline generator yields images that follow detailed prompts more faithfully and with richer texture and structure.
layout: 2 rows by 5 columns, baseline above ours, prompt captions below with bold-underlined key phrases
description: A 2×5 grid of generated images. The top row is labeled BAGEL and the bottom row is labeled UNO, with rotated labels on the left. Each column shows the same prompt rendered by both models. The subjects are a fantasy nature spirit blended with a waterfall, a knight's armor made of transparent crystal glass filled with roses, two glowing semi-transparent birds on a crystal branch, an impressionist wildlife photo of an animal filling the frame, and a futuristic chrome and iridescent guitarist. Italic prompt text sits under each column. Key phrases that the baseline misses are in bold and underlined, for example 'made of transparent crystal glass'. The UNO row follows these phrases more closely: it is more transparent, richer in detail and more vivid. The eye goes first to the saturated images.
caption: Qualitative comparisons on image generation between BAGEL and BAGEL-UNO.
abstract: Unified multimodal models are envisioned to bridge the gap between understanding and generation. Yet, to achieve competitive performance, state-of-the-art models adopt largely decoupled understanding and generation components. This design, while effective for individual tasks, weakens the connection required for mutual enhancement, leaving the potential synergy empirically uncertain. We propose to explicitly restore this synergy by introducing Understanding-Oriented Post-Training (UNO), a lightweight framework that treats understanding not only as a distinct task, but also a direct supervisory signal to steer generative representations. By incorporating objectives that encode semantic abstraction (captioning) and structural details (visual regression), we enable effective gradient flow from understanding to generation. Extensive experiments on image generation and editing demonstrate that understanding can serve as an effective catalyst for generation.
